title: Space Operations Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC I
raw_text:
19.     MOS 8866, Space Operations Officer (I) (LtCol to 2ndLt) FMOS, DC I

    a. Summary. Space Operations Officers are tasked with representing the
Marine Corps interest in national security space matters, to include
participating in the development of space plans, policy, doctrine, and
requirements. Space Operations Officers will be expected to make
recommendations to decision makers regarding the employment of space systems
in support of operational plans, the acquisition of space systems, and the
development of space architectures to support Marine Corps needs.

    b. Prerequisites. Security requirement: SCI security clearance
eligibility. Must have a current T5 investigation and adjudicated for SCI
eligibility.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Space Systems Operations Curriculum Number 366
(Space Systems Operations) or Curriculum Number 591 (Space Systems
Engineering) at the Naval Postgraduate School, Monterey, California.
Additional approved sources of education include curriculums GSS (Graduate
Space Systems) and GA (Graduate Astronautical Engineering) from the Air Force
Institute of Technology, Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio.

                (a) Completed a thesis on a topic relating to space operations.

            (b) Earned a masters degree in Space Systems Operations,
Astronautical Engineering, or a related field.

        (2) Space operations officers must have a comprehensive practical and
theoretical knowledge of space policy and doctrine, the space environment,



                                           1-360                     Enclosure (1)
 1147                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



and space relevant technologies.         Further, they must have specific detailed
knowledge of:

                (a) Orbital mechanics.

                (b) Simulation and modeling.

                (c) Acquisition management.

                (d) Joint doctrine for space operations.

                (e) The Joint operational planning process.

                (f) National reconnaissance office (NRO) overhead systems.

            (g) Mission requirements that drive spacecraft design
requirements.

            (h) Plans, concepts, strategies, and tactics for employment of
space systems.

            (i) Great power competition in space, approaches to space
security, and the major space treaties and policy debates to include the
impact of the commercial and civil sectors on space security.

            (j) Organization and responsibilities of national security space
to include the department of defense and the intelligence community.

            (k) Military space operations and associated capabilities to
include space situational awareness, space control, position, navigation, and
timing, intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance, satellite
communications, environmental monitoring, missile warning, nuclear detonation
detection, space lift and launch, and satellite operations.

    d. Duties. Supervise or support other space operations Marines.
Maintain understanding of all MOS 1786 requirements; assist with tasks as
required.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Atmospheric and Space Scientists 19-2021.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Maritime Space Officer, 1706.

            (2) Basic Information Planner, 1781.

            (3) Space Operations Staff Officer, 1786.

            (4) Special Technical Operations Officer, 8016.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade.
